summary: Defines how ForCES messages are carried over SCTP, the Transport Mapping Layer for ForCES. It explains why SCTP was chosen and how it meets the requirements. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: ForCES needs a delivery truck, and this explains why a certain truck was picked and how packages go on it.

subtitle: How ForCES control and forwarding elements talk over SCTP, using three prioritized channels.

tldr.problem: The ForCES protocol layer needs a transport underneath that offers reliability, congestion control, prioritization, high availability and security between control elements and forwarding elements.
tldr.mechanism: The SCTP TML opens three SCTP sockets per CE-FE pair, on ports 6704, 6705 and 6706, for high-priority reliable, medium-priority semi-reliable and low-priority unreliable traffic, and serves them with strict priority scheduling. IPsec provides security.
tldr.outcome: A single transport covers every TML requirement of RFC 5810, and tying node overload to transport congestion keeps important work moving under load.

today: RFC 5811 is a Proposed Standard, and its metadata shows no later RFC obsoleting or updating it. It is the SCTP mapping for the ForCES protocol of RFC 5810.

sections.title: Where the TML Fits
sections.content:
The ForCES (Forwarding and Control Element Separation) working group defines how control elements (CEs) and forwarding elements (FEs) inside a network element such as a router communicate. The protocol layer (PL), specified in RFC 5810, handles protocol semantics. It runs on top of an interconnect-hiding layer called the Transport Mapping Layer (TML).

Only one PL is defined, but different TMLs are expected, and the TML at the CE and FE must be of the same definition to interoperate. The PL hands messages to the TML, which delivers them to the destination TML. This document defines the SCTP-based TML and shows how it meets the TML requirements in Section 5 of RFC 5810.
sections.eli5: The ForCES language is the same everywhere, but there are different ways to carry it. This note describes one carrier, SCTP.

sections.title: Why SCTP
sections.content:
SCTP, defined in RFC 4960, is like TCP in providing ordered, reliable, connection-oriented, flow-controlled and congestion-controlled exchange, but it keeps message boundaries instead of a byte stream. Like UDP it can be unreliable and unordered, though it has no multicast. Like DCCP it can be unreliable, ordered and congestion controlled.

The RFC adds features it found attractive: multi-homing, runtime IP address binding, a range of reliability shades with congestion control, built-in heartbeats, multi-streaming, message boundaries with reliability, improved SYN DOS protection, simpler transport events and simplified replicasting. Because one transport can satisfy all TML requirements, there is no need for several, which allows simpler coding and reduces interoperability concerns.
sections.eli5: SCTP can do a bit of everything the other carriers do, plus extras. Picking just one carrier keeps life simple.

sections.title: Three Channels, Three Sockets
sections.content:
The TML opens three SCTP sockets between any two PL endpoints. Each is a channel with its own port and Payload Protocol ID (PPID):

  • High priority, reliable (HP): port 6704, PPID 21. Carries AssociationSetup, AssociationSetupResponse, AssociationTeardown, Config, ConfigResponse, Query and QueryResponse, with PL priorities 4 to 7.
  • Medium priority, semi-reliable (MP): port 6705, PPID 22, using SCTP partial reliability with a time limit per message. Carries Event Notification at PL priority 3, suited to events that are cumulative and recoverable by a query.
  • Low priority, unreliable (LP): port 6706, PPID 23, also partial reliability with lower timeouts than MP. Carries PacketRedirect (priority 2) and Heartbeat (priority 1).

A message with a priority, PPID or type that does not belong on a channel MUST be dropped. A response MUST carry the same priority as its request.

The authors first planned one socket with three streams, but found head-of-line blocking: low-priority packets not needing reliable delivery could block high-priority reliable ones under congestion. Hence three separate sockets.
sections.eli5: There are three mail slots: one with certified delivery, one that gives up on stale mail, and one for throwaway mail. Each kind of note goes in the right slot.

sections.title: Strict Priority Scheduling and Overload
sections.content:
The TML core uses strict priority, work-conserving scheduling: HP messages are processed until none remain, then MP, then LP. Under congestion, a busy higher-priority channel can starve lower ones. The scheduling is receiver-based, so some reordering across channels is tolerable. What matters is that the CE gets to a high-priority message soon rather than spending long periods on redirected OSPF packets.

This ties node overload to transport congestion. If an FE is busy with config requests from the CE, it essentially ignores the LP channel, and redirected packets that accumulate are dropped because the LP threshold is exceeded or because they are obsoleted. SCTP congestion control then propagates the pressure back to the source.

The FE SHOULD connect the channels in increasing priority (LP, then MP, then HP). The CE MUST NOT assume any connection order. The appendices suggest per-FE and per-CE work orders and note that NE-level scheduling across many peers is left to the implementation, with fairness and robustness against denial of service as concerns.
sections.eli5: The worker always empties the urgent slot first. If there is too much mail, the junk slot overflows and gets thrown away, and the senders slow down.

sections.title: Meeting the TML Requirements
sections.content:
Section 4.2.2 walks through the RFC 5810 requirements:

  • Reliability and congestion control: SCTP offers shades of reliability and has congestion control built in.
  • Timeliness and prioritization: three sockets plus partial reliability.
  • Addressing: no extra headers are needed. The TML translates PL addresses into unicast IP addresses to emulate multicast and broadcast PL addresses.
  • High availability: multi-homing gives path diversity, heartbeats and transmission thresholds detect faults per peer address, and ADDIP can migrate addresses at runtime, not unlike VRRP, when moving activity from one FE or CE to another.
  • Node overload prevention: the strict priority design above.
  • Encapsulation: the PPIDs identify the channel.

Parameters such as IP addresses, whether to use IPsec, and the three ports are supplied through the FE Manager or CE Manager interface.
sections.eli5: The RFC takes a checklist of what the carrier must do and shows that SCTP can do each item, such as switching roads if one road breaks.

sections.title: Security with IPsec
sections.content:
The TML offers transport-level authentication of CEs and FEs, message authentication, and confidentiality, using IPsec. The operator chooses all, some or none of these during the pre-association phase, and may turn security off in a secured environment.

A CE or FE MUST support IKE with certificates for endpoint authentication, transport mode ESP, HMAC-SHA1-96 for integrity, AES-CBC with 128-bit keys for confidentiality, and replay protection. Implementations SHOULD allow negotiating other cipher suites and manual keying.

To keep configuration small, the RECOMMENDED selector in the Security Policy Database is just SCTP protocol number 132, needing a single SPD and SAD entry. Using the three port numbers as selectors is allowed but requires more entries.
sections.eli5: A lock and a secret handshake protect the notes in transit, and the owner can choose how many locks to use.

sections.title: Assigned Ports and PPIDs
sections.content: The IANA section lists SCTP port 6704 for the HP channel, 6705 for MP and 6706 for LP. It also lists SCTP Payload Protocol IDs 21 (ForCES-HP), 22 (ForCES-MP) and 23 (ForCES-LP).
sections.eli5: Each mail slot gets its own number so everyone knows which is which.

items.label: HP channel
items.desc: Reliable. Config, Query, association messages; PL priorities 4 to 7.

items.label: LP channel
items.desc: Unreliable with shorter timeouts. PacketRedirect and Heartbeat; PL priorities 2 and 1.
